headToHead.voiceVerdict: Tie, up from a clear loss. Cover the names on our twelve and every one is Pixel by shape, not noun: the chat quote in lowercase then a two-word ruling, the score with a deduction, the self-interrupting drop, the counting. Polly is equally unmistakable (self-answered question, 'So,' 'Anyway,' death misread as gossip). The tie holds only for the top twelve; across the bank 45 percent of lines lose the shape, and Polly's shape carries a worldview (death is small talk) while Pixel's carries a format (a Twitch overlay).
headToHead.constructionVerdict: Tie. Ours is tighter: median 8 words against Polly's 20-plus, turn on the last word, nothing explains itself, while Polly has flab ('kick this party up a notch, huh?') and one self-explainer ('ghostsip as I like to call it'). But five of our twelve borrow the punch from the rival's cast sheet (processing fee, press zero for a support menu, pop-up ad, golden retriever, Quill not finishing); Polly builds every turn from her own appetite by escalation and literalism, which is the harder and more renewable engine.
headToHead.quotableVerdict: Bar. 'Fun back in funeral', 'so hard to keep track of what kills people', 'hot people are always right' and 'hay bbe lez party' travel with no context. Of ours only 'Ending stream before I get bored of ending stream' and maybe 'Massive moth' survive without the suitor on screen; 'Six, minus the processing fee' and 'person or a menu' are good clips that need Prince and Tilly to land.

notes: The bar file existed and was read in full; Polly's lines are verbatim from it, and two of her twelve are player options written for her events (flagged). Real progress since round 1: chat is now quoted with content 18 times (was once), the drop is down to one use (the moth), the Frost and fridge lines are all rewritten for Crumb, scores mostly carry a condition, and the generic share fell from 58.6 to 45.0 percent (86 of 191 lines). The fix overshot: chat is in 30 percent of lines and is now the tag on the end of everything, and Pixel too often agrees with chat instead of overruling it. I want to see how many you have.'); it should be the engine of the cuts and one-on-ones, which are currently the weakest slots.
